summary: No Huánuco-specific signal was identified in the sources reviewed, and the national assessment for Peru applies to visitors to the department: the material available documents no departmental law, enforcement practice, recorded incident or institution bearing on trans visitors.
tangentialFactors: The sources examined for Huánuco are national in scope: congressional records on the 2025 public-facility restriction, a legal analysis by the human-rights institute of the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru, and the annual report of the TLGBI rights observatory at Universidad Peruana Cayetano Heredia. None disaggregates restroom-access rules, discrimination complaints or homicide figures to the department, so no departmental pattern adjacent to the national picture can be set out here.
localsOnly: Nothing specific to trans residents of Huánuco was located. The material found on public-facility access, identity-document recognition and recorded violence against trans people addresses Peru as a whole, and gives no department-level detail on services, police conduct or venue policy in Huánuco.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether police, prosecutors and commercial venues in Huánuco apply Peru's national provisions in the same manner as those in Lima, and whether any Huánuco case has been brought under them, is unresolved; no department-level incident, complaint or enforcement record appeared in this review.

Recorded violence data on trans people in Peru are compiled nationally and name specific Lima locations in the cases they detail; the departmental distribution for Huánuco is not published in the sources available, so no rate for the department can be stated.
